To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of tocotrienol and tocopherol mixed fraction with vitamin C supplementation did not improve lipid and inflammatory biomarkers in hypercholesterolemia patients with moderate coronary disease.
the combination of TTMF plus vitamin C supplementation did not show any added benefit in lowering lipid profiles and inflammation in statin-treated patients with HC.
combination of TTMF with vitamin C supplementation leads neutral effects on inflammation and lipid profiles in non-statin treated HC patients with moderate cardiovascular risk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of tocotrienol and vitamin C as a dietary supplement to improve the lipid profile and reduce inflammatory biomarkers in patients on statin treatment.
the potential beneficial effects of TTMF+C supplementation in HC patients with moderate risk.
the effects of adding TTMF and C supplementation on coronary biomarker levels in patients with HC and moderate coronary risk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of TTMF plus vitamin C supplementation has no significant effect on lipid and inflammatory biomarkers in statin-treated patients with moderate coronary risks.
the combination of TTMF+C supplementation does not have any added benefits to the existing statin therapy for the treatment of patients with HC and moderate coronary risk.
TTMF supplementation is neutral in the management of lipid profiles and inflammation in statin-treated patients with hypercholestrolaemia with moderate coronary disease risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TTMF+C supplementation is safe to be used as an alternative to statins in non-statin-treated HC patients with low to moderate coronary risk.
TTMF+C supplementation alone is not beneficial for HC patients with moderate risk and that the addition of atorvastain to TTMF+C is also not beneficial.
TTMF+C supplementation is not effective in reducing inflammation and lipid profiles in HC with moderate coronary risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
combination of TTMF with atorvastain in statin-treated patients with HC and moderate coronary risk may not provide any additional benefits in lipid profiles and inflammation.

the combination of TTMF+C does not provide additional benefit over statins for lipid and inflammatory profiles, and may not be recommended as a complementary therapy in patients with moderate coronary disease.
the use of TTMF+C in non-statin-treated HC patients with coronary risk may be a useful adjunct therapy to reduce inflammation, and thus, may be beneficial for patients who are unable to take statins.
